S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

patient_info.stressor: When Diego Camacho changed into a new technical college program tied to advanced CNC training, he suddenly faced unfamiliar classmates, shop-floor evaluations, ID photos, and more online collaboration than he had expected. In that setting, an appearance concern that had once been an occasional embarrassment became a central preoccupation with a perceived defect that others did not see as significant. His repeated appearance-related routines increasingly displaced sleep, class preparation, soccer, and STEM volunteering, and he began missing labs and shop shifts because getting out the door felt tied to whether he could make himself look acceptable. After a faculty mentor noticed the absences and Diego’s work placement was put at risk, he met with campus counseling and was referred for a psychiatric assessment.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I came in because I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks off, like my nose and jaw are crooked in every ID photo or online class camera, and even when people say they don’t see it I feel like everyone in the CNC lab is noticing it before they notice my work.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before I leave for school I get stuck checking my face in the bathroom mirror and my phone camera, fixing my hair or changing shirts to hide the angle, asking my mom if it looks weird, and sometimes I do it so long that I miss lab or show up too wiped out to focus.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve missed CNC labs and shop shifts because I couldn’t get myself out the door, and now my faculty mentor says my work placement could be in jeopardy. I also stopped playing soccer and volunteering because I don’t want people looking at me.
